lxc_c56e9c784458b9af.text: The strangest fruit combinations in real food are surprising mixes of fruit with meat, fish, chili, cheese, or salt, not a fruit salad.

lxc_82a1deb2e4e3b944.text: Their flavors may sound unusual, but each mix has a clear idea behind it.

lxc_72ebf31a3f6724c7.text: A useful way to understand these foods is to notice three things: the fruit, its partner, and the final result.

lxc_a7a5a1dcd4ecfb4e.text: Melon with ham is a clear starting point.

lxc_f5b95287f5a3cb00.text: It is a specialty in Spanish, Italian, and French cooking, usually served in spring and summer.

lxc_a984d2fc181aa2f2.text: The plate contains melon and slices of ham.

lxc_232714c0e1ebe4cb.text: The ham may be serrano ham from Spain, Bayonne ham from France, or another salty ham.

lxc_0c507b8d61231b81.text: In prosciutto e melone, the Italian name for this pairing, sweet melon meets salty cured ham.

lxc_60d5cc43c37769a9.text: The fruit and meat stay separate and easy to recognize.

lxc_e8fe18ce67e4fd78.text: The surprising result comes from the strong difference between their flavors.

lxc_057abd70a325b2db.text: Some combinations place fruit inside a rich meat dish.

lxc_89e95004ca222088.text: Duck à l’orange is a French dish of roast duck with bigarade sauce, a sauce made with bitter Seville oranges.

lxc_4458bab54431c24c.text: Its main ingredients include duck, orange, butter, stock, sugar, and vinegar.

lxc_cf71d5bec9eb4dd7.text: The first published recipe appeared in 1813 in The French Cook.

lxc_842d7c4de634c7ef.text: Fesenjan is a sweet-and-sour Iranian stew from Gilan.

lxc_1ecd22ef13e6eb80.text: It is a khoresh, an Iranian stew served over rice.

lxc_b55141d771a36667.text: Its main mix is pomegranate juice or paste, ground walnuts, and poultry such as duck or chicken.

lxc_d76addd2fe865ca1.text: It can also contain other meats.

lxc_addc429cb07aa56c.text: Unlike melon with ham, the fruit becomes part of the sauce and gives flavor to the whole dish.

lxc_a95d721d4b432ffa.text: Green papaya salad shows that a fruit dish does not need to be sweet.

lxc_492022fc9604ff8a.text: It is a spicy salad made from shredded unripe papaya.

lxc_1728418cb9abc299.text: In Thailand it is called som tam, the Thai name for this sour, salty, and spicy salad.

lxc_28f34e135ace5026.text: The mix includes sour lime, hot chili, salty fish sauce, and a little palm sugar.

lxc_6b24dbe2df41334f.text: Dried shrimp may also be included.

lxc_c978d8651246dbbd.text: Chamoy offers another surprising use of fruit.

lxc_9f16307f76d4b66c.text: Chamoy is a Mexican sauce made from pickled fruit, salt, and chili.

lxc_92d26dc37c2ab9c7.text: Fruit is packed in brine, which is salty water used for pickling, sometimes with vinegar.

lxc_6595fb2d29dc16fe.text: The fruit brine is then seasoned with chili powder.

lxc_132eab330ab80b71.text: The finished sauce can be put on fresh fruit, adding salty, sour, sweet, and spicy flavors.

lxc_e37f3721224667f3.text: Hawaiian pizza is a Canadian pizza with pineapple, tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and ham or bacon.

lxc_dad6cdd712c1d6f8.text: Sam Panopoulos is credited with making the first one at the Satellite Restaurant in Ontario in 1962.

lxc_ef52168188b2238e.text: He tried the mix because Canadian Chinese dishes often combine sweet and sour flavors.

lxc_3a20e14cd5907326.text: The name came from the canned pineapple brand he used, not from the state of Hawaii.

lxc_921d476fa7f01cee.text: Romeu e Julieta is a traditional Brazilian pairing of cheese and goiabada, a thick guava conserve.

lxc_0e83e29c8dea669c.text: The simplest plate is guava conserve on a slice of cheese.

lxc_cc43b85e2b9a1181.text: It is believed to have begun in Minas Gerais during the colonial period.
